title: How does a fallen log rot away?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How long does a log take to rot?
Why are dead logs good for wildlife?

explain.say: When a big tree falls, it does not lie there forever. Over years or decades, living things eat it away until all that is left is rich, dark soil.

draw.text: How does a fallen log rot away?

explain.say: First, fungal spores and wood-boring beetles get in through the bark. Fungal threads spread through the wood, releasing enzymes that dissolve its tough cellulose and lignin.
As the wood softens, more creatures move in: woodlice, millipedes, ants, slugs and worms. Mosses, seedlings and animals use the rotting log as food and shelter.
Rotting is fastest at first and slows as only the toughest parts remain, so the wood left falls along a decay curve. A twig can vanish in a few years; a giant log may take a century or more.

faq.a: Mainly fungi, which can digest the cellulose and lignin that make wood tough, helped by bacteria, beetles, termites and other wood eaters. Water and warmth speed them up.

faq.q: What is the difference between white rot and brown rot?
faq.a: White-rot fungi break down lignin, the dark, stiff part of wood, leaving it pale and stringy. Brown-rot fungi eat the cellulose and leave the lignin, so the wood turns brown and cracks into cubes.
asks: Why is some rotten wood white?

faq.q: Why are dead logs good for nature?
faq.a: A rotting log is home and food for fungi, beetle grubs, woodlice, mosses and many more. Foresters often leave dead wood on purpose to support wildlife.
asks: Should dead trees be left in the forest?

faq.q: How long does a log take to rot?
faq.a: It depends on its size, the kind of wood and the climate. Twigs can rot in a few years, while big logs in cool forests can take a hundred years or more.

faq.q: Why does rotting slow down over time?
faq.a: The easiest parts of the wood to eat are used up first. What remains is tougher, so it takes longer and longer to break down, which makes a decay curve.
asks: Why does a log rot slower at the end?

facts: Fungi are the main decomposers of wood because they can break down lignin and cellulose.
Large fallen logs in cool forests can take a century or more to rot completely.
White-rot fungi leave wood pale and stringy; brown-rot fungi leave it brown and cracked into cubes.

quiz.say: Which living things do most of the work of rotting wood?
quiz.show: Which living things do most of the work of rotting wood?
quiz.why: Fungi release enzymes that can digest the tough cellulose and lignin in wood.

wrong.1: Birds may peck at logs for grubs but do not digest wood.
wrong.2: Grass may grow on rotted wood but does not break it down.
